headline: OpenAI has added a Windows 11 sandbox to Codex, its coding agent, that isolates the commands the agent runs without needing administrator setup.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a useful tool change for developers on Windows 11, narrow in reach and with an open bug.
importance_line: What changed: developers on compatible Windows 11 PCs can limit what an AI coding agent may read, write or reach on the network without an administrator setting it up; it does not run on every PC, and users have already reported a start-up failure linked to BitLocker.
summary: Nerd's Chalk reports, citing OpenAI's announcement of 9 Oct 2026, that the new Codex mode uses Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), a Windows feature that applies file and network limits to a command and the processes it starts, with no administrator approval, extra Windows accounts or firewall rules. It works only on compatible Windows 11 PCs, Codex includes a test command to check support, and a bug report opened on 4 Oct 2026 describes MXC failing to start when an unrelated drive is locked by BitLocker, Windows disk encryption.
notes: Read from fulltext. OpenAI's announcement is quoted in the article; the original post link was not given.
